chunks: Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:

He was asked about a man who performed the obligatory tawaf and did not perform the two rakʿahs until he had performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Then he performed tawaf al-nisāʾ and did not perform the prayer for that tawaf until he remembered while he was at al-Abṭaḥ. He said: He should return to the Maqām and perform two rakʿahs.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs of prayer required after tawaf
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: the two known locations between which saʿy is performed
key_terms.الْأَبْطَحِ: the place where the person remembered the omitted prayer
key_terms.الْمَقَامِ: Maqām Ibrāhīm, the place to which one returns for the tawaf prayer
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: the tawaf whose completion restores marital permissibility
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory tawaf that must be performed as part of the rite

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he forgot the two rakʿahs of tawaf until after saʿy and tawaf al-nisāʾ?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who forgot the two rakʿahs of tawaf even after proceeding through later rites of hajj or ʿumrah. The Imam عليه السلام rules that he must return to the Maqām and perform the two rakʿahs, showing the continuing obligation of the prayer associated with tawaf.
